sources.text:
- Gujarati News
- International
- Air Canada Flight Crash At LaGuardia Airport; Many Injured | NYC
ન્યૂયોર્ક એરપોર્ટ પર વિમાન-ટ્રકની ટક્કર, બંને પાયલોટના મોત:એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલરે સ્ટોપ-સ્ટોપ બૂમ પાડી, 72 મુસાફરો સવાર હતા
- કૉપી લિંક
અમેરિકાના ન્યૂયોર્કમાં લા ગાર્ડિયા એરપોર્ટ પર રવિવારે રાત્રે (સ્થાનિક સમય મુજબ) એર કેનેડા એક્સપ્રેસનું એક વિમાન લેન્ડિંગ સમયે રનવે પર ફાયર ટ્રક સાથે અથડાયું. આનાથી વિમાનનો આગળનો ભાગ સંપૂર્ણપણે નાશ પામ્યો.
આ દુર્ઘટનામાં પાયલટ અને કો-પાયલટનું મૃત્યુ થયું, જ્યારે ટ્રકમાં સવાર બે લોકો ઘાયલ થયા. જાઝ એવિએશન અનુસાર, આ ફ્લાઇટ મોન્ટ્રિયલથી આવી રહી હતી.
CRJ-900 વિમાનમાં કુલ 72 મુસાફરો અને 4 ક્રૂ મેમ્બર સવાર હતા.ટક્કરના તરત જ બાદ રનવે 4 બંધ કરી દેવામાં આવ્યો. એરપોર્ટ પર ઇમરજન્સી લાગુ કરીને તમામ ફ્લાઇટ ઓપરેશન રોકી દેવામાં આવ્યા અને આવનારી ફ્લાઇટ્સને ડાયવર્ટ કરવામાં આવી.
દુર્ઘટના પહેલા એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલરે વિમાન અને ગ્રાઉન્ડ વાહન બંનેને રોકાવા માટે કહ્યું હતું અને 'સ્ટોપ-સ્ટોપ' બૂમો પાડતો રહ્યો, પરંતુ તેમ છતાં ટક્કર થઈ.
દુર્ઘટનાનો વીડિયો જોઈ લો...
ટેક્સીવે પર દુર્ઘટના
શરૂઆતી રિપોર્ટ મુજબ, આ પ્લેન એર કેનેડા એક્સપ્રેસની ફ્લાઇટ AC8646 હતી, જે એક બોમ્બાર્ડિયર CRJ-900 જેટ છે. તેને જાઝ એવિએશન ઓપરેટ કરે છે. જણાવવામાં આવી રહ્યું છે કે પ્લેન રનવે 4/22 પાસે એક ટેક્સીવેને પાર કરતી વખતે ફાયર ટ્રક સાથે અથડાયું. ઘટનાસ્થળેથી મળેલા પ્રારંભિક ફોટામાં પ્રાદેશિક જેટના આગળના ભાગને ઘણું નુકસાન દેખાઈ રહ્યું છે, જે દર્શાવે છે કે ટક્કર જોરદાર હતી. ઇમરજન્સી ટીમો પહોંચતા જ મુસાફરોને પ્લેનમાંથી ઉતાવામાં આવ્યા. ઓનલાઈન વાઇરલ થઈ રહેલી એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલ (ATC)ની રેકોર્ડિંગમાં ટક્કરના બરાબર પહેલા ટ્રકને 'રોકો' (stop)ની ચેતવણી આપવામાં આવી રહી છે. આ જ કારણોસર એક ડેલ્ટા ફ્લાઇટને લેન્ડિંગ કરતા રોકી દેવામાં આવી.
એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલરે વિમાનને રોકવાનો પ્રયાસ કર્યો હતો
લેન્ડિંગ પહેલાં એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલરે વિમાનને રોકવાનો પ્રયાસ કર્યો હતો. વાઇરલ ઑડિયોમાં એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલરે પહેલાં ટ્રકને રનવે પાર કરવાની મંજૂરી આપી હતી, પરંતુ થોડી જ વાર પછી કંટ્રોલર સતત “સ્ટોપ, સ્ટોપ, ટ્રક 1” બૂમો પાડતો રહ્યો. જોકે, થોડી જ સેકન્ડમાં ટક્કર થઈ ગઈ.
કંટ્રોલરનો અવાજ રેકોર્ડિંગમાં સંભળાય છે- “JAZZ 646, તમે વાહન સાથે અથડાયા છો, ત્યાં જ રોકાઈ રહો, મદદ પહોંચી રહી છે.”
ફ્લાઇટ લેન્ડિંગ પછી રનવે પર લગભગ 130 માઇલ પ્રતિ કલાકની ઝડપે આગળ વધી રહી હતી. સોશિયલ મીડિયા પર વાઇરલ વીડિયોમાં વિમાનના આગળના ભાગમાં નુકસાન અને કૉકપિટ ઊંચકાયેલું દેખાઈ રહ્યું છે.
એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલની વાઇરલ થયેલી રેકોર્ડિંગ સાંભળો…
ઇમરજન્સી રિસ્પોન્સ અને એરપોર્ટ બંધ
દુર્ઘટના બાદ, અમેરિકી અધિકારીઓએ આ મોટા ટ્રાન્સપોર્ટ હબ પર તમામ ફ્લાઇટ્સ પર પ્રતિબંધ મૂક્યો. ફેડરલ એવિએશન એડમિનિસ્ટ્રેશનએ ફ્લાઇટ્સ રોકવાનું કોઈ કારણ જણાવ્યું નથી, પરંતુ કહ્યું કે આ આદેશ આગળ વધવાની 'પૂરી સંભાવના' છે.
રિપોર્ટ્સ અનુસાર, ઇમરજન્સી સેવાઓ તરત જ ટેક્સીવે પર તૈનાત થઈ ગઈ, જેથી પરિસ્થિતિનો તાગ મેળવી શકાય અને પ્લેનમાં સવાર લોકોને મદદ કરી શકાય. એવી અપેક્ષા છે કે નેશનલ ટ્રાન્સપોર્ટેશન સેફ્ટી બોર્ડ (NTSB), FAA સાથે મળીને આ ટક્કરની તપાસ કરશે. અધિકારીઓ ઘટના સમયેના એર ટ્રાફિક કંટ્રોલ કમ્યુનિકેશન, એરક્રાફ્ટ મૂવમેન્ટ ડેટા અને એરપોર્ટ વાહનોની સ્થિતિની તપાસ કરશે. આ દુર્ઘટના એવા સમયે થઈ છે જ્યારે સમગ્ર અમેરિકાના એરપોર્ટ્સ સ્ટાફની અછતનો સામનો કરી રહ્યા છે, ખાસ કરીને ટ્રાન્સપોર્ટેશન સિક્યુરિટી એડમિનિસ્ટ્રેશન (TSA) ના કર્મચારીઓની.

Odrzutowiec Air Canada Express zderzył się z pojazdem naziemnym tuż po wylądowaniu na lotnisku LaGuardia w Nowym Jorku w niedzielę wieczorem lokalnego czasu. Nie żyją dwaj piloci samolotu. Do szpitali trafiło ponad 40 osób. Incydent spowodował zamknięcie lotniska.
- Odrzutowiec Air Canada Express zderzył się z pojazdem naziemnym na lotnisku LaGuardia w Nowym Jorku.
- Federalna Administracja Lotnictwa USA (FAA) wstrzymała starty i lądowania na lotnisku LaGuardia.
- Najnowsze informacje z kraju i ze świata na rmf24.pl.
Samolot CRJ-900, który przyleciał z Montrealu, uderzył w pojazd strażacki z prędkością około 24 mil na godzinę (39 km/h) - podał Flightradar24. Odrzutowiec był obsługiwany przez Jazz Aviation, regionalnego partnera Air Canada - informuje Reuters.
Według oficjalnych informacji dwie osoby nie żyją. Pilot i drugi pilot samolotu zginęli.
Łącznie 41 osób, w tym pasażerów, członków załogi oraz funkcjonariuszy służb ratowniczo-gaśniczych lotniska, przewieziono do szpitali - poinformowała dziennikarzy dyrektor wykonawcza lotniska Kathryn Garcia. 32 osoby już zwolniono. Niektóre są "poważnie ranne" - dodała Garcia.
Na pokładzie samolotu znajdowało się 72 pasażerów i czterech członków załogi, a samolot był na końcowym etapie lądowania - podaje NBC News.
Federalna Administracja Lotnictwa USA (FAA) wydała zakaz startów i lądowań dla wszystkich samolotów na tym lotnisku.
W komunikacie FAA wskazano, że powodem zatrzymania ruchu na lotnisku był stan awaryjny i istniało duże prawdopodobieństwo jego przedłużenia, bez podawania szczegółów.
Strona internetowa LaGuardii informowała, że samoloty przylatujące zostały przekierowane na inne lotniska lub zawrócone do punktu startu.
W osobnym komunikacie dla pilotów FAA podała, że lotnisko może pozostać zamknięte do godziny 18:00 GMT.
Nowojorska Straż Pożarna w oświadczeniu poinformowała, że reaguje na zgłoszony incydent z udziałem samolotu i pojazdu na pasie startowym lotniska LaGuardia, ale nie podała dalszych szczegółów.

sources.news_title: Air Canada Plane & Fire Truck Collide At LaGuardia, Causing Major Accident
sources.text:
A terrible tragedy happened, and unfortunately there are fatalities. While I covered this earlier, I’d like to provide a bit of an update, based on the information that has come out in the hours following the accident.
In this post:
Air Canada Jazz CRJ-900 & fire truck have fatal accident
At around 11:40PM on Sunday, March 22, 2026, an Air Canada Jazz CRJ-900 and a fire truck collided on runway 4 at New York LaGuardia Airport (LGA). The plane belonging to Air Canada’s regional subsidiary was just landing on runway 4 from Montreal Airport (YUL), and was moving around 100 miles per hour at the time of impact.
The CRJ-900 ended up with its nose in the air, and the plane’s cockpit largely destroyed. Meanwhile the fire truck ended up over in the grass and on its side, and was barely identifiable. Air Canada’s CRJ-900s have 76 seats, with a crew of four (including two pilots and two flight attendants). This particular flight had 72 passengers, so it was nearly full.
It has now been revealed that the captain and first officer both passed away, and some of the firefighters are critically injured. It remains to be seen how many serious injuries there are beyond that. My thoughts are with those onboard and their families, and in particular, with those who lost their lives. Following the incident, LaGuardia Airport was closed, given rescue efforts.
How did this LaGuardia Airport accident happen?
To state the obvious, both planes and ground vehicles need permission in order to move around airports, given what congested spaces they are. So what exactly happened here? It would appear that this was an air traffic control error.
Listening to air traffic control audio from the accident, while the Air Canada Jazz CRJ-900 was landing on runway 4, the air traffic controller also gave the fire truck permission to cross the runway.
The fire truck had requested permission from the tower controller to cross the runway — “Truck 1 and company, LaGuardia tower, requesting to cross 4 at delta.” The air traffic controller granted that permission — “Truck 1 and company, cross 4 at delta.”
After a short while, the controller realized the error — “stop, stop, stop, stop, stop, Truck 1, stop, stop, Truck 1, stop.” Unfortunately at that point it was too late, though, and the plane and the fire truck had collided.
Ugh, for all the close calls we see, here’s one that didn’t end well. Reports suggests that the controller was working alone. Admittedly LaGuardia isn’t that busy overnight, but air traffic controllers certainly have stressful jobs, and even a small mistake can have major consequences, as we’re seeing here.
For added context, the controller was trying to assist with another emergency at the same time. United flight UA2384 was scheduled to fly to Chicago (ORD), and had two rejected takeoffs. The pilots of that flight declared an emergency, and requested fire trucks, so the air traffic controller seemed to be largely focused on that. In a comment to another pilot after the accident, the controller said “we were dealing with an emergency earlier, and I messed up.”
Bottom line
An Air Canada Jazz CRJ-900 and a fire truck collided on a LaGuardia runway, after an air traffic controller accidentally cleared the fire truck onto the runway while the other plane was landing. He was busy dealing with another emergency. The scenes from the accident look awful, and it has been confirmed that the two pilots lost their lives, and firefighters are critically injured.
My thoughts are with those involved and their families, and I’m hoping for as few serious injuries and fatalities as possible. I also feel bad for the controller making an honest mistake — I can’t imagine how he’s feeling right now. Air traffic controllers have really gotten the short end of the stick in recent years, in terms of an immense workload due to short staffing. Of course at some point that’s going to impact performance. Never mind that he was dealing with another emergency.

sources.news_title: Air Canada jet hits vehicle, forcing New York’s LaGuardia airport to close
sources.text:
An Air Canada Express regional jet struck a Port Authority vehicle on the ground after landing at New York’s LaGuardia Airport late Sunday night, killing two people and forcing the airport to close.
The CRJ-900 plane, which was arriving from Montreal, struck the vehicle at about 24 miles per hour shortly before midnight, according to flight tracking website Flightradar24.
Two pilots were killed in the incident, Port Authority Executive Director Kathryn Garcia said at a news briefing. More than 40 passengers, crew members and Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) officers were transported to the hospital, she said.
“At this time, we understand that 32 have been released, but there are also serious injuries,” Garcia said. “Sadly, the two pilots are confirmed deceased and notifications are being made by Air Canada’s care team at this time.”
The jet was operated by Jazz Aviation, Air Canada’s regional partner. Air Canada and Jazz Aviation confirmed the incident to Fox News Digital.
“Flight 8646 was en route to LGA from Montréal (YUL),” Jazz Aviation said in a statement to Fox News Digital. “The preliminary passenger list indicates the aircraft was carrying 72 passengers and 4 crew members, although this is subject to confirmation. The incident occurred at approximately 11:47PM on March 22, 2026.”
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop for all planes at the airport, saying there was an emergency without offering specific details. The airport is expected to be closed until 2 p.m. Monday, the FAA said.
LaGuardia’s website showed arriving planes had been diverted to other airports or returned to where they took off from.
The Port Authority confirmed that the jet collided with a Port Authority Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting vehicle.
“At approximately 11:40 p.m. on Sunday, a Jazz Aviation flight operating on behalf of Air Canada was involved in an incident on Runway 4 at LaGuardia Airport in which the aircraft struck a Port Authority Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting vehicle that was responding to a separate incident,” a Port Authority spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital.
“Emergency response protocols were immediately activated,” the statement continued. “The Port Authority Police Department is on scene along with the agency’s Chairman and Executive Director. The airport is currently closed to facilitate the response and allow for a thorough investigation.”
The spokesperson added: “This is a developing situation based on preliminary information. The Port Authority Police Department is working closely with our airline partners as well as federal authorities, and will provide additional updates as more details become available.”
U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy’s office also confirmed to Fox News Digital that the flight crashed with a Port Authority fire truck at LaGuardia Airport after the plane landed late Sunday night and that the flight included four crew members — the captain, first officer and two flight attendants.
The New York Fire Department said in a statement that it was responding to an incident involving a plane and a vehicle on the runway at LaGuardia Airport, although it did not provide additional details.
The New York City Police Department confirmed the collision but did not offer further information.
Multiple videos taken at the scene showed the jet with severe damage to the front of the aircraft.
The National Transportation Safety Board said it is “launching a go team to investigate the March 22 Jazz Aviation, Air Canada Express Flight 8646, CRJ900, airplane that collided with a fire truck on Runway 4 at LaGuardia Airport in New York.”
Fox News Digital reached out to the FAA, NTSB and LaGuardia Airport for additional information.
The New York City Office of Emergency Management said travelers should expect road closures, traffic delays and cancellations near the airport.
SOUTHWEST FLIGHT DIVERTED AFTER PASSENGER SCARE AS SECURITY INCIDENTS RATTLE US AIRPORTS
Air Canada said it was setting up a phone line for loved ones of the passengers to call for assistance. The number was: 1-800-961-7099.
The incident came amid weekslong turmoil at airports across the country amid a funding lapse for the Department of Homeland Security, which has caused long lines and left Transportation Security Administration (TSA) employees working without being paid for more than a month.
Some TSA workers have quit and security lines at many airports left travelers waiting for hours. U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents are slated to deploy to airports Monday to help the TSA.
Reuters and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: LaGuardia operations halted after plane collides with ground vehicle - OrissaPOST
sources.text:
New York: Operations at New York’s LaGuardia Airport were suspended after an Air Canada Express CRJ-900 aircraft collided with a ground vehicle on Runway 4, triggering an emergency response and a complete ground stop.
The aircraft, operated by Air Canada Express and arriving from Montreal, reportedly struck a fire truck during landing, according to initial accounts and flight-tracking data.
The Federal Aviation Administration confirmed that the airport has been closed and that a ground stop order has been implemented following the collision between the aircraft and the emergency vehicle.
Audio recordings circulating online, along with preliminary visual reconstructions, suggest that air traffic control had repeatedly instructed both the flight crew and the ground vehicle to halt moments before the impact occurred.
Unconfirmed reports, citing the New York Fire Department, indicate that at least five firefighters have been seriously injured, while more than 100 passengers on board the aircraft are also reported to have sustained injuries.
Emergency response teams, including Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) units, remain deployed at the site.
Initial information points to multiple injuries, including several firefighters and passengers, with some described as being in critical condition, although officials have not yet released final figures.
Following the incident, the Federal Aviation Administration imposed a ground stop on all incoming and outgoing flights at the airport to facilitate emergency operations and begin an investigation into the cause of the collision.

sources.text:
To døde da Air Canada-fly krasjet med kjøretøy på New York-flyplass
Et regionfly har kollidert med et kjøretøy på flyplassen LaGuardia i New York etter landing, bekrefter brannvesenet og politiet i den amerikanske storbyen. To skal være døde, melder NBC news.
Søndag kveld kolliderte et fly med en brannbil på en av New Yorks flyplasser.
Flyet er et Bombardier CRJ-900 fra Air Canada Express. Nettstedet FlightRadar24, som overvåker verdens flytrafikk, meldte om hendelsen først.
Brannbilen rykket ut for å assistere et annet fly, hvor det hadde vært en ukjent lukt i cockpiten.
Det ble et dødlig krasj for piloten og co-piloten i flyet. I tillegg ble de to som satt inni brannbilen skadet.
Ni passasjerer er på fortsatt på sykehus.
Starter etterforskning
I et opptak i kommunikasjonen fra kontrolltårnet kan man høre at brannbilen får tillatelse til å krysse flybanen. Bare sekunder etterpå gir kontrollpersonalet beskjed om at bilen må stoppe.
«Bil en, stopp, stopp, stopp!» sier en kontrollør før vedkommende sier at de ser at de har krasjet.
Ifølge offisielle rapporter var det 41 passasjerer på sykehus, hvorav ni er på sykehus nå. Det var totalt 72 passasjerer på flyet.
En rekke videoer tatt av øyevitner og publisert i sosiale medier viser at flyet har store skader i fronten. Hendelsen fant sted kl. 23.38 lokal tid søndag.
Flyet kjørte i over 200 km i timen før den traff brannbilen, skriver CNN.
Trafikken ved den minste av New Yorks tre hovedflyplasser er stanset, og flyplassen er stengt. Den skal være stengt frem til 14.00 mandag.
Den amerikasnske etaten for national transport sikkerhet skal sette i gang en etterforskning av hendelsen.

LaGuardia-flyplassen sendte sent søndag ut et varsel om at regn og overskyet vær kunne forstyrre driften ved flyplassen.
Flyplassen åpner for avgang på den ene rullebanen mandag klokken 14.00 lokal tid.

sources.news_title: New York LaGuardia Airport Closed After Plane Collides With Fire Truck
sources.text:
A mass casualty incident was declared at New York City's LaGuardia Airport following a ground collision between a commercial aircraft and an emergency vehicle. According to airport officials, an Air Canada Express CRJ-900 aircraft, carrying approximately 100 passengers, collided with a fire truck on the runway. The incident prompted an immediate suspension of all airport operations and a large-scale emergency response.
Preliminary reports indicate that the collision resulted in serious injuries to 5 emergency personnel who were inside the fire truck at the time of impact. While the aircraft sustained visible damage, all passengers were successfully evacuated from the plane and moved to a secure area near the runway. No fatalities have been confirmed by authorities as of the latest update.
Collision Near Runway 4 During Taxiing
The accident took place near Runway 4 while the Air Canada Express flight was taxiing across the airfield. According to media reports, the CRJ-900 was moving along its designated path when it struck the fire department vehicle. The impact caused significant damage to the aircraft's structure, while rescue teams and additional fire units were dispatched to the site immediately to secure the area and prevent any potential fire hazards from the damaged vehicles.
Condition of Emergency Personnel and Rescue Efforts
The 5 emergency workers involved in the crash were reported to be in serious condition and were transported to local hospitals for urgent medical treatment. Rescue operations focused on extracting the injured personnel from the fire truck and ensuring the safety of the 100 passengers on board the flight. Medical teams evaluated passengers for minor injuries and psychological distress following the abrupt collision on the tarmac.
Impact on Airport Operations and Flight Diversions
Following the incident, LaGuardia Airport was officially closed to all incoming and outgoing traffic. Aviation authorities redirected all inbound flights to John F. Kennedy (JFK) International Airport to manage the air traffic flow. The closure has led to significant delays and cancellations across the regional aviation network. Airport management is working to clear the runway and assess the safety of the infrastructure before resuming operations.
ATC Communications and Preliminary Investigation Details
Reports have emerged regarding Air Traffic Control (ATC) audio recordings from the time of the incident, while according to these claims, ATC officials had instructed the fire truck to stop and hold its position. However, the vehicle allegedly continued onto the active taxiway, leading to the collision with the aircraft, while investigators are currently analyzing the communication logs to determine why the instructions weren't followed and if there were any technical failures in the radio systems.
Damage Assessment and Safety Protocols
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) have launched a formal investigation into the ground collision. The investigation will focus on the coordination between ground vehicles and aircraft, as well as the adherence to safety protocols at the airport. Maintenance crews are also inspecting the runway surface for any damage caused by the impact and the subsequent fuel or fluid leaks from the vehicles involved.

All arriving flights have been diverted or forced to return to their origin.

El incidente fue confirmado por la Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA) de Estados Unidos a las 23.40 del domingo. La entidad comunicó que se suspendieron todos los vuelos programados del aeropuerto debido a una “emergencia aérea”.
El vuelo afectado fue el AC-8646 de Jazz Aviation LP -operado por Air Canada Express-, proveniente del Aeropuerto Internacional Pierre Elliott Trudeau, en Montreal, Canadá, con 72 pasajeros a bordo y cuatro tripulantes. Se trataba de un jet modelo CRJ-900 utilizado para vuelos de corto y mediano alcance.
Enseguida se activaron los protocolos de seguridad: los bomberos de la ciudad respondieron al incidente para rescatar a los pasajeros y al personal de a bordo que estaban atrapados en el interior del fuselaje, que se vio comprometido, informó CNN.
“LaGuardia está cerrado”, escribió la FAA en su sitio web. “Los vuelos con destino a LaGuardia están suspendidos debido a una emergencia relacionada con un avión”, añadió la autoridad de aviación, sin brindar más detalles. La investigación se centra en determinar en qué circunstancias el camión de asistencia de la Autoridad Portuaria ingresó a la pista.
Jazz Aviation LP emitió un comunicado confirmando el accidente. La aerolínea dijo que una lista preliminar de pasajeros, sujeta a confirmación, indicaba que había 72 pasajeros y cuatro miembros de la tripulación a bordo.
Varios videos tomados por testigos y publicados en redes sociales mostraron el avión con graves daños en la parte delantera de la aeronave. Las imágenes muestran el avión de Air Canada gravemente dañado iluminado por reflectores y vehículos de emergencia estacionados cerca en la pista.

sources.news_title: Deadly Collision Paralyzes New York’s LaGuardia Airport
sources.text:
The bustling, tightly constrained tarmac of New York’s LaGuardia Airport has been violently transformed into a catastrophic disaster zone following a horrific collision between a commercial passenger jet and a heavy emergency response vehicle. In a devastating breakdown of ground control protocols, Jazz Airlines Flight 646—operating as an Air Canada Express Canadair Regional Jet CRJ-900 arriving from Montreal—slammed directly into an airport firetruck while actively navigating the taxiways near Runway 4. The sheer kinetic force of the impact severely crushed the nose and front fuselage of the regional jet, instantly killing at least two individuals and leaving dozens of terrified passengers and first responders with critical injuries.
The immediate aftermath of the catastrophic impact plunged the major New York transit hub into absolute chaos. Early audio leaks and preliminary flight-tracking data suggest a terrifying sequence of miscommunication, with air traffic controllers reportedly shouting repeated instructions for both the aircraft crew and the massive Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting (ARFF) vehicle to immediately halt mere moments before the violent collision. The heavy, armored structure of the firetruck ripped directly into the fragile aluminum skin of the CRJ-900, trapping passengers in a nightmare of crushing metal on the active tarmac.
New York Fire Department units rapidly surged onto the runway, declaring a mass-casualty incident. Emergency personnel immediately initiated desperate extraction protocols to pull bleeding and deeply traumatized passengers from the shattered wreckage of the Canadian jet. Initial reports from ground crews suggest several firefighters sustained severe, “red tag” injuries during the initial impact, while scores of passengers aboard the aircraft were violently thrown upon collision. The sheer scale of the localized devastation forced the Federal Aviation Administration to instantly execute a complete ground stop, entirely shutting down all inbound and outbound flight operations at LaGuardia and sending immediate, cascading delays throughout the entire North American airspace network.
As federal investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board urgently scramble to the heavily restricted crash site, the fundamental safety architecture of one of America’s busiest airports is under intense, unforgiving scrutiny. The terrifying reality that a commercial airliner could successfully land, only to be violently intercepted and destroyed by the very emergency vehicles tasked with protecting it, points to a catastrophic failure in situational awareness and surface-level radar monitoring. As emergency convoys continue to lock down the Queens airport to tend to the wounded, the entire commercial aviation sector is bracing for the horrifying final casualty count of this entirely preventable, deadly tarmac disaster today.

sources.news_title: Air Canada plane hits ground vehicle at New York’s LaGuardia Airport
sources.text:
‘I messed up’: Footage shows Air Canada jet hit fire truck as controller panicked
Updated ,first published
New York: Air-traffic controllers were helping a fire truck’s crew navigate a rain-slicked tarmac at New York’s LaGuardia when panic suddenly set in.
The crew had been summoned to inspect a United Airlines jet preparing to take off before midnight on Sunday (New York time). The drama that followed would quickly become the latest in a series of deadly US aviation disasters.
“Stop, stop, stop, stop, Truck 1, stop, stop, stop,” a controller can be heard saying about 11.37pm. “Stop, Truck 1, stop! Stop, Truck 1, stop!” the controller continues, becoming increasingly frantic.
A voice that sounds like the same controller then instructs an arriving Delta Air Lines plane to perform a go-around, an aviation manoeuvre in which a pilot aborts landing and climbs back to a safe altitude. The controller quickly turns to an Air Canada Express plane operated by Jazz Aviation, acknowledging that the aircraft had struck a truck on the ground.
“I see you collided with a vehicle there. Just hold position. I know you can’t move. Vehicles are responding to you now,” he said.
Almost 20 minutes later, a person appearing to be the same controller can be heard discussing the airport’s closure following the collision with a pilot of a Frontier Airlines flight.
“That wasn’t good to watch,” the pilot can be heard saying over air traffic audio.
The controller replies that he tried to get the truck to stop, adding, “We were dealing with an emergency earlier. I messed up.”
The Air Canada Express CRJ-900 plane, operated by its regional partner Jazz Aviation, was carrying 72 passengers and four crew members from Montreal, said Kathryn Garcia, the executive director of the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey.
Social media footage showed the moment of impact as the fire truck crossed into the aircraft’s path as it landed, destroying its cockpit and forward fuselage. The plane was travelling at more than 200 km/h at the moment of impact, according to law enforcement sources.
Photos and videos from the scene showed severe damage to the forward section, with cables and debris hanging from a mangled cockpit. Nearby, a damaged emergency vehicle lay on its side.
Both the pilot and co-pilot were pronounced dead at the scene. Another 41 people were transported to hospital, according to the Port Authority.
One flight attendant was thrown from the aircraft, still strapped into the jump seat, and was found by police on the runway, a senior law enforcement official told Bloomberg.
Flight attendant Solange Tremblay suffered multiple fractures to one leg and will need surgery, her daughter, Sarah Lépine, told Canadian news station TVA Nouvelles, describing her survival as “a total miracle”.
“I’m still trying to understand how all this happened, but she definitely has a guardian angel watching over her,” Lépine told the station.
Passenger Rebecca Liquori said the plane hit turbulence while descending, and she then felt it brake hard and heard a loud boom.
“Everybody just jolted out of their seats. People hit their heads. People were bleeding,” Liquori told News12 Long Island.
Liquori, who said she helped open the emergency exit door, recalled passengers helping each other slide down a wing to get out.
“I’m just happy to be alive,” said Liquori, who had gone to Montreal for a cousin’s baby shower. “I would have never pictured a one-hour flight that I’ve done countless times … ending like this.”
Another passenger described chaos in the moments after the crash. “Everybody was hunkered down, everybody was screaming,” Jack Cabot told WABC-TV, adding that they weren’t getting instructions because the flight deck had been destroyed.
“So somebody said, ‘let’s get the emergency exit and get the door and let’s all jump out’, and that’s exactly what we did.”
Controllers under scrutiny
A key part of the crash investigation will be examining the co-ordination of the airport’s air traffic and ground traffic at the time of the crash, said Mary Schiavo, a former Department of Transportation inspector-general.
“This has been happening for years, and sadly, some of the most horrific air crashes in history happen on the ground at the airport.”
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said LaGuardia was “well-staffed” but still faced a shortage of air-traffic controllers. He said there were 33 certified controllers, but the goal was to have 37. More than one controller was on duty at the time of the accident, he said.
“I can’t give specifics on what went wrong,” Duffy said, deferring to the National Transportation Safety Board, which is leading the inquiry. Canada has also sent a team of investigators.
The crash closed LaGuardia – the New York region’s third-busiest hub – during what was already a difficult time at US airports because of a partial government shutdown.
Flights resumed on Monday afternoon (US time) on one runway, with lengthy delays. The closure caused some disruptions at other airports, too, especially for Delta, which has a major presence at LaGuardia.
The tragedy follows a string of fatal aviation disasters last year, including a midair collision between a regional commercial jet and a US Army helicopter outside Washington that killed 67 people and a fiery UPS freighter crash that resulted in the deaths of more than a dozen people onboard the aircraft and on the ground.
There have been many previous incidents of planes colliding with catering trucks and other vehicles while taxiing, but these events often occur at very low speeds and rarely result in fatalities.
These events are placed under a broad category of safety incidents known as runway incursions, which can range from relatively benign events such as a pilot edging slightly past painted lines they’re supposed to stop at before entering a runway, but there aren’t any landing or departing aircraft in the vicinity that pose an immediate safety risk to more serious situations, such as collisions.
The US Federal Aviation Administration disclosed 97 runway incursions in January, according to the most recently available data posted on its website.
Bloomberg, AP, Reuters

sources.news_title: Breaking: Air Canada CRJ-900 Collides With Fire Truck At LaGuardia, 2 Fatalities Reported
sources.text:
Last Updated: 05:10 AM EST MAR 23, 2026 by Luke Bodell
An Air Canada Express Bombardier CRJ-900 has collided with a fire truck at LaGuardia Airport (LGA), with reports suggesting at least two fatalities and dozens of critical injuries. Early images of the accident reveal significant damage to the regional jet's cockpit, nose and front fuselage.
The collision reportedly occurred near LGA's Runway 04 as the aircraft was performing its landing while a fire truck was simultaneously cleared to cross the runway. The airport has now suspended all operations as emergency services tend to the injured.
National Air Traffic Controllers Association Comments On Crash
Monday, March 23rd, 15:30 PM EST
The National Air Traffic Controllers Asssociation (NATCA) has issued a statement on the LaGuardia crash. NATCA said it was "deeply saddened by the tragic accident at LaGuardia Airport between an Air Canda Jazz CRJ-900 and an emergency vehicle on the ground," adding, "Our hearts are with the victims, their families, and all those affected during this incredibly difficult time. We extend our sincere condolences and stand in support of the entire aviation community including our brothers and sisters with the Air Line Pilots Association (ALPA) and the Canadian Flight Attendant Union (CFAU: SABC) who have been affected by this tragedy."
Pilot And Co-Pilot Confirmed Dead
Monday, March 23, 5:10 AM EST
Initial reports of the accident stated there were two deaths, but it was not clear if these fatalities were among the passengers, crew or occupants of the fire truck. Various media outlets in the US are now reporting that both the pilot and co-pilot of the Air Canada Express jet died in the accident.
NBC News adds that a sergeant and officer occupying the truck are being treated for broken limbs at a local hospital, but are in a stable condition. The fire truck involved in the accident was being dispatched to another aircraft at LaGuardia when the tragedy occurred. This is being reported as United Flight 2384, which had rejected takeoff and subsequently reported an odor in the cabin and requested emergency services.
Air Canada CRJ-900 Smashes Into LaGuardia Fire Truck
Monday, March 23, 12:34 AM EST
At least two people have reportedly been killed after Jazz Airlines Flight 646, an Air Canada Express service from Montreal, collided with a fire truck while landing at LaGuardia on Sunday night. According to Flightradar24 data, the aircraft had landed at 11:37 PM local time following a one-hour flight from Montréal–Trudeau International Airport (YUL).
Images of the aftermath reveal catastrophic damage to the front of the CRJ-900, which had tipped back onto its tail, leaving its gnarled cockpit and front fuselage in an elevated position. Along with the two reported fatalities, five more individuals are said to be critically injured, with as many as 70 injuries among passengers. Critical injuries have also been reported among the firefighters occupying the truck. The on-duty controller said the following as the accident unfolded:
"Stop, stop, stop, stop. Stop Truck 1. Stop.... Jazz 646? Jazz 646, I see you collided with a vehicle there. Just hold position."
Fire Truck Cleared To Cross Runway
Air traffic control (ATC) recordings reveal that the fire truck, identified as Truck 1, requested clearance to cross Runway 04 at Delta, which was granted. However, moments later, a controller frantically ordered the truck to stop as Flight 646 was speeding along the runway. Following the collision, an incoming Delta jet was ordered to go around as the controller attempted to establish communications with the Jazz Airlines pilots.
As reported by aviation insider JonNYC on X, the on-duty controller had been working on his own at the time of the accident, overseeing both ground and tower operations. The controller was reportedly "dealing with another emergency at the time," which the fire truck had been dispatched to.
Flightradar24 data shows that the CRJ-900's last recorded ground speed was 21 kts, although its speed at the time of impact will almost certainly have been much higher. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has issued a ground stop at LaGuardia following the accident, grinding all operations to a halt.
Inbound flights have now been diverted to nearby airports, including New York JFK (JFK) and Newark (EWR). According to the Port Authority of NY & NJ, LaGuardia sees an average of over 400 flights per day. Passengers in the New York area have been warned to expect flight cancellations and delays due to the knock-on effect of LGA's closure.
Delta Connection Bombardier CRJ900s Collide At LaGuardia Airport, Leaving 1 Injured
The incident involved an outbound flight for Roanoke and an inbound flight from Charlotte.
About The Aircraft Involved
The plane involved in Sunday night's accident is a 20-year-old CRJ-900 (registration: C-GNJZ) operated by Jazz Air on behalf of Air Canada Express. The regional jet can accommodate up to 76 passengers in two cabin classes, with 12 in business and 64 in economy.
The aircraft had departed Montreal more than two hours and 30 minutes later than its scheduled 7:59 PM departure time, eventually setting off at 10:35 PM. The flight to LaGuardia took just over an hour, with the jet touching down at 11:37 PM local time.
Now almost certain to be written off, the CRJ-900 was first delivered to Air Canada Jazz in November 2005, and is equipped with two GE CF34-8C5 engines.

sources.news_title: Aeroplane Crash in Ny, and Two Pilots Die
sources.text:
Um avião da Air Canada colidiu com um caminhão de bombeiros na pista do aeroporto LaGuardia, em Nova York, nos Estados Unidos, na noite de domingo (22). O incidente matou duas pessoas, o piloto e o copiloto da aeronave, e deixou dezenas de feridos.
A Administração Federal de Aviação dos EUA emitiu uma ordem de interrupção de solo para todos os aviões no aeroporto, que cancelou as operações. A previsão é que o aeroporto permaneça fechado até a tarde desta segunda (23).
O avião CRJ-900, da Air Canada, operado por sua parceira regional Jazz Aviation, transportava 72 passageiros e quatro tripulantes vindos de Montreal, no Canadá, disse Kathryn Garcia, diretora-executiva da Autoridade Portuária de Nova York.
Ela informou que 32 dos 41 feridos já haviam recebido alta, enquanto nove permaneciam hospitalizados com "ferimentos graves".
A aeronave colidiu com o caminhão de bombeiros, que estava atendendo a outro incidente, por volta das 23h40 do horário local.
O veículo, pertencente à autoridade portuária de LaGuardia, pediu permissão para cruzar a pista. Um áudio da torre de comando, divulgado pelo site de monitoramento Live ATC, revelou o momento da colisão.
Logo após o controlador autorizar a circulação do caminhão, ele pede que o motorista pare. "Pare, pare, pare, caminhão 1 pare, caminhão 1, pare", diz a voz na gravação. O veículo, porém, não responde ao comando.
Segundo o site de rastreamento de voos Flightradar, o avião estava a uma velocidade de aproximadamente 39 hm/h quando colidiu com o veículo. Fotos do acidente mostram danos visíveis na parte frontal da aeronave, que estava inclinada para cima.
Minutos após a batida, um controlador diz na gravação: "Aquilo não foi bom de ver". O controlador que estava em contato com o caminhão responde: "Sim, eu sei. Eu estava aqui. Eu tentei entrar em contato… Estávamos lidando com uma emergência antes. Eu errei."
"Não, cara, você fez o melhor que pôde", afirma o outro funcionário no áudio.
A autoridade portuária informou que o caminhão de bombeiros estava respondendo a outra aeronave, da United Airlines, que havia relatado "um problema de odor" dentro da cabine. Os controladores informaram à tripulação que um caminhão de bombeiros já estava a caminho.
O Conselho Nacional de Segurança nos Transportes dos EUA informou que enviaria uma equipe de especialistas técnicos para investigar o incidente. Segundo especialistas, a investigação deve analisar se havia funcionários suficientes no controle de tráfego aéreo, as ações do controlador e da equipe do caminhão naquela noite, além da posição do veículo.
O LaGuardia, localizado no bairro de Queens, em Nova York, é o terceiro aeroporto mais movimentado da cidade e atendeu 33,5 milhões de passageiros em 2024, segundo dados da autoridade portuária.
O aeroporto passou, em 2024, por uma renovação de US$ 8 bilhões (cerca de R$ 40 bilhões) para modernizar sua infraestrutura envelhecida, com novos terminais e pistas.

sources.news_title: Pilot and Co-Pilot Die when Plane Hits Truck at New York Laguardia Airport
sources.text:
NUEVA YORK - Un avión de Air Canada chocó el domingo por la noche con un vehículo de la Autoridad Portuaria después de aterrizar en el Aeropuerto LaGuardia, según las autoridades. El accidente causó la muerte del piloto y el copiloto de la aeronave, así como heridas a dos agentes de la Autoridad Portuaria, de acuerdo con fuentes de NBC.
El impacto dejó la aeronave inclinada hacia arriba con el morro aplastado, mientras los funcionarios trabajaban para confirmar los detalles del accidente.
“Aproximadamente a las 11:40 de la noche del domingo, un vuelo de Jazz Aviation que operaba en nombre de Air Canada estuvo involucrado en un incidente en la Pista 4 del Aeropuerto LaGuardia en el que la aeronave golpeó un vehículo de Rescate de Aeronaves y Extinción de Incendios de la Autoridad Portuaria que estaba respondiendo a un incidente distinto”, dijo la Autoridad Portuaria de Nueva York y Nueva Jersey en un comunicado.
El comunicado señaló que la policía de la Autoridad Portuaria y el presidente y director ejecutivo de la agencia estaban en el lugar en la pista del aeropuerto, que cerró mientras se investigaba el accidente.
"El piloto y el copiloto del vuelo de Jazz Aviation fueron declarados muertos. Además, 41 personas fueron trasladadas al hospital: 39 personas que se encontraban a bordo de la aeronave y dos oficiales del ARFF. El aeropuerto permanecerá cerrado hasta al menos las 2:00 p. m. del lunes para permitir la realización de una investigación exhaustiva", según la Autoridad Portuaria de Nueva York y Nueva Jersey.
La Autoridad Portuaria de Nueva York y Nueva Jersey dijo en un comunicado que el avión había golpeado un vehículo de rescate y extinción de incendios que estaba respondiendo a un incidente distinto aproximadamente a las 11:45 de la noche. El aeropuerto cerró a partir de las 3 de la madrugada para facilitar la investigación, dijeron los funcionarios.
Fotos y videos de la escena mostraron graves daños en la parte delantera de la aeronave, con cables y escombros colgando de una cabina destrozada. Cerca, un vehículo de emergencia dañado yacía de lado.

Otra de las fuentes indicó que una revisión preliminar realizada por los equipos de emergencia revela que el avión había recibido autorización para aterrizar, y que el camión también contaba con autorización para cruzar la pista. La NTSB deberá verificar este dato en el marco de su investigación para determinar si un error de comunicación tuvo parte de la culpa en el suceso.
Dos fuentes señalaron a NBC News que el avión impactó contra la parte central del camión, lo que provocó que los agentes que viajaban en la parte delantera salieran despedidos del vehículo, permitiéndoles, no obstante, sobrevivir. El morro del avión se encontraba en una posición baja, por lo que los pilotos recibieron la fuerza total del impacto.

sources.news_title: Vehicle Crash at New York Laguardia Airport; Report Injured
sources.text:
Deja Dos Muertos y 41 Heridos Choque de Avión en Aeropuerto LaGuardia de Nueva York
N+
Un piloto y su copiloto murieron por el choque de un avión con un camión en el aeropuerto LaGuardia de Nueva York, donde fueron suspendidos los vuelos; 41 personas resultaron heridas
COMPARTE:
Al menos dos personas murieron por el choque de un avión de Air Canada con un vehículo de la Autoridad Portuaria tras aterrizar en el aeropuerto LaGuardia de Nueva York, cuyo accidente obligó a suspender los vuelos en el lugar.
Las víctimas mortales son dos pilotos, informó Kathryn Garcia, directora ejecutiva de la Autoridad Portuaria de Nueva York y Nueva Jersey. Ambos tenían su base en Canadá. La funcionaria añadió que al menos 41 personas fueron llevadas al hospital, pero 32 han sido dadas de alta.
Los dos agentes que iban en el camión de bomberos que colisionó con el avión se encuentran en estado estable en el hospital, agregó Garcia en conferencia de prensa.
La Administración Federal de Aviación (FAA, por sus siglas en inglés) informó que no habrá vuelos con origen ni destino en el aeropuerto de LaGuardia hasta las 14:00 horas de este lunes, tiempo local.
La aerolínea confirmó que en el avión iban 72 pasajeros y cuatro tripulantes. Mientras que el aeropuerto de LaGuardia indicó que el impacto fue contra un vehículo de rescate y extinción de incendios de aeronaves de la Autoridad Portuaria que estaba respondiendo a un incidente aparte.
El Departamento de Policía de Nueva York confirmó la colisión y un portavoz del Departamento de Bomberos de "la gran manzana" dijo que los vulcanos respondieron a los reportes de un avión que se estrelló contra un vehículo en la pista a las 23:38 horas, tiempo local.
"El aeropuerto permanece cerrado para facilitar la respuesta y permitir una investigación exhaustiva. Esta situación está en desarrollo según la información preliminar. El Departamento de Policía de la Autoridad Portuaria está colaborando estrechamente con nuestras aerolíneas asociadas y con las autoridades federales", señaló el aeropuerto precisando que los hechos ocurrieron a las 23:40 horas del domingo 22 de marzo.
(1/2) Nous avons pris connaissance d'un incident concernant le vol Air Canada Express 8646 du 22 mars 2026, opéré par Jazz Aviation LP (Jazz), reliant Montréal à New York LaGuardia. Consultez le communiqué de presse de Jazz ici.
— Air Canada (@AirCanada) March 23, 2026
"Jazz Aviation LP ('Jazz'), que opera como Air Canada Express, confirma que se ha producido un incidente en el que se ha visto involucrado el vuelo AC8646 operado por un CRJ900 en LaGuardia (LGA)"; se indicó en un boletín emitido por Air Canada.
"El vuelo 8646 se dirigía al aeropuerto LGA desde Montreal (YUL). La lista preliminar de pasajeros indica que la aeronave transportaba 72 pasajeros y 4 tripulantes, aunque esta información está pendiente de confirmación. El incidente ocurrió aproximadamente a las 23:47 del 22 de marzo de 2026", añadió.
Noticia relacionada: Choque en Aeropuerto LaGuardia: Aviones se Impactan a Baja Velocidad en Nueva York
Varios videos grabados por transeúntes y publicados en las redes sociales mostraban el avión con graves daños en la parte delantera que quedó prácticamente desecha y con la estructura doblada. Cables y escombros quedaron colgando de una cabina destrozada. Cerca, un vehículo de emergencia dañado yacía de lado.
At approximately 11:40 p.m. on Sunday, a Jazz Aviation flight operating on behalf of Air Canada was involved in an incident on Runway 4 at LaGuardia Airport in which the aircraft struck a Port Authority Aircraft Rescue and Firefighting vehicle that was responding to a separate…
— LaGuardia Airport (@LGAairport) March 23, 2026
¿Cómo fue el accidente?
El camión de bomberos estaba cruzando la pista para responder a un incidente distinto a bordo de un vuelo de United Airlines, cuyo piloto había reportado "un problema con olor", dijo Garcia, quien remitió preguntas adicionales sobre la secuencia de eventos que condujeron al choque a la Junta Nacional de Seguridad en el Transporte de Estados Unidos (NTSB, por sus siglas en inglés).
El choque se dio en la pista 4 cuando la aeronave CRJ-900 de Air Canada aterrizaba. El vuelo había salido del Aeropuerto Internacional Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau, el principal aeropuerto que sirve a Montreal.
Según Flightradar24, la aeronave impactó contra el vehículo a una velocidad de aproximadamente 39 km/h. El avión era operado por Jazz Aviation, socio regional de Air Canada.
Se habían llevado escaleras para evacuar a los pasajeros de las aeronaves por las salidas de emergencia del avión, un Bombardier CRJ. El impacto dejó al avión inclinado hacia arriba sobre el morro aplastado.
En los momentos previos al accidente, se pudo escuchar a un controlador de tráfico aéreo en una transmisión de radio dando autorización a un vehículo para cruzar parte de la pista, y luego tratando de detenerlo.
"Deténgase, Camión 1. Deténgase", dice la transmisión. Luego se puede escuchar al controlador desviando frenéticamente a las aeronaves entrantes para que no aterricen.
Envían equipo de investigación y desvían vuelos
La Junta Nacional de Seguridad en el Transporte de Estados Unidos indicó que creó un equipo de investigación para indagar sobre el accidente del vuelo 8646 de Jazz Aviation que colisionó con un camión de bomberos.
"La presidenta Jennifer Homendy actuará como portavoz en el lugar del evento, acompañada por el miembro John DeLeeuw. Se espera que el equipo de investigación llegue hoy", señaló.
NBC indicó que un sargento y un oficial tienen extremidades fracturadas y se encuentran en condición estable en un hospital. Además, se precisó que la unidad impactada es un camión de bomberos operado por agentes de policía.
El sitio web de LaGuardia mostraba que los aviones que llegaban habían sido desviados a otros aeropuertos o habían regresado a su punto de origen.
Due to an emergency incident at LaGuardia Airport, all streets and highway exits into the airport are closed until further notice. Expect delays and avoid the area if possible. pic.twitter.com/UnZ50X01Hk
— NYPD NEWS (@NYPDnews) March 23, 2026
A primera hora de este lunes, algunos pasajeros que habían llegado a LaGuardia horas antes de sus vuelos con la esperanza de evitar las filas de seguridad durante el actual lapso de financiación del gobierno fueron saliendo del aeropuerto, después de que sus viajes se reprogramaran para el martes.
Otros se dirigían a aeropuertos alternativos, tan lejos como Long Island MacArthur en el suburbio de Ronkonkoma, para tratar de tomar sus vuelos.

sources.news_title: Ny: Air Canada Plane Collides with Fire Truck
sources.text:
Colisión entre avión y camión en NY deja varios heridos
Una colisión entre una aeronave comercial y un camión de bomberos en el Aeropuerto LaGuardia desencadena evacuación de pasajeros y heridos graves.
Una colisión entre una aeronave comercial y un camión de bomberos se registró la noche de este domingo 22 de marzo en el Aeropuerto LaGuardia, en Estados Unidos, lo que provocó la movilización de cuerpos de emergencia y la suspensión de operaciones.
Accidente en pista 4 de LaGuardia
De acuerdo con reportes preliminares, el incidente ocurrió en la pista 4 poco antes de la medianoche, cuando un avión tipo CRJ-900 de la aerolínea Air Canada Express colisionó con una unidad del Departamento de Bomberos de Nueva York.
La aeronave transportaba a cerca de 100 pasajeros. Tras el impacto, se reportó la evacuación de los ocupantes hacia la pista, mientras que los primeros informes indican al menos cinco personas con heridas graves. También se reporta que cuatro bomberos que viajaban en el camión resultaron lesionados de gravedad.
Versiones iniciales señalan que habría al menos dos personas fallecidas; sin embargo, hasta el momento esta información no ha sido confirmada oficialmente, mientras continúan las labores de rescate y evaluación en el sitio.
Condiciones y respuesta oficial
El choque ocurrió cuando el avión se dirigía a una puerta de embarque, en medio de condiciones meteorológicas adversas que ya habían provocado interrupciones en vuelos horas antes. Imágenes difundidas muestran severos daños en la parte frontal de la aeronave, especialmente en la cabina.
Tras el incidente, la Administración Federal de Aviación ordenó el cierre temporal del aeropuerto, lo que derivó en cancelaciones y retrasos en vuelos de llegada y salida.
Asimismo, el Departamento de Bomberos de Nueva York activó una segunda alarma para atender la emergencia, lo que implicó un despliegue ampliado de unidades y personal en la zona.
Las autoridades iniciaron investigaciones para esclarecer las causas del accidente. De manera preliminar, se menciona la posibilidad de un error en el control de tráfico terrestre, aunque esta hipótesis no ha sido confirmada.
El incidente se suma a una jornada complicada en aeropuertos de Estados Unidos, donde previamente se habían reportado afectaciones por condiciones climáticas adversas.
